question: In how many years will ₹50,000 become ₹66,550 at 10% compound interest per annum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate = 10% = 1/10 ⇒ Multiplying factor per year = 11/10

Ratio of Amount to Principal = 66550 ÷ 50000 = 1331 ÷ 1000

We know that (11/10)³ = 1331 / 1000

Since the cube corresponds to 3 periods, the time taken is 3 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹50,000

Amount (A) = ₹66,550

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% per annum

**Formula Used:**

A = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

 Total Time = 3 Years

**Calculations:**

⇒ 66,550 = 50,000 × (1 + 10/100)ⁿ

⇒ 66,550 ÷ 50,000 = (1 + 1/10)ⁿ

⇒ 6,655 ÷ 5,000 = (11/10)ⁿ

⇒ 1,331 ÷ 1,000 = (11/10)ⁿ

⇒ (11/10)³ = (11/10)ⁿ

⇒ n = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of CI

For a 10% annual interest rate, the effective CI rate for 2 years is 21%, and for 3 years it is 33.1%. Here, 33.1% of ₹50,000 exactly equals the interest of ₹16,550.

Difference between CI and SI (2 Years)

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for a period of 2 years is calculated directly as: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Difference between CI and SI (3 Years)

For a period of 3 years, the formula extends to: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (3 + R ÷ 100).
